credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.

Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}, taking gross leverage down by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.

Cash generation strengthened: FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, lifting FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}}, and free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}.
FCF to debt rose by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}, while capex intensity fell by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.
Interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, still well above the peer median.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity fell by the same proportion to {{cash_liquidity@FY2024}}.
Cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}}.
In FY2023 the group reported liquidity of {{liquidity@FY2023}}, including {{undrawn_facilities@FY2023}} of undrawn committed credit facilities.

Fitch raised Aena's long-term and EMTN programme rating and its short-term rating with a stable outlook, and Moody's moved the outlook to positive while confirming the long-term and EMTN programme ratings.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, with traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} below the {{traffic_growth@FY2023}} of FY2023.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, with the CNMC setting the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged on the prior year.
The concession of the Rafael Núñez International Airport in Cartagena ended during the year, and the result includes the gain on the sale of ADI's stake in ESSP SAS.

peer_positioning.text: Aena has the highest EBITDA margin of the airport peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2024}}, and leads the group on FFO to debt ({{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}) and FCF to debt ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}).
Leverage sits in the middle of the group, with net leverage ranking {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}} and gross leverage {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}.

Cash liquidity to revenue is the weakest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} against a median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2024}}.

snapshot.text: Aena, the Spanish airport operator, had a stronger FY2024 as revenue rose by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} and both Fitch and Moody's moved its ratings in a positive direction.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}, with the EBITDA margin widening by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}.
The point to watch is cash liquidity, which fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} of revenue, the weakest of the airport peers.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, the lowest of the airport peers, as cash and cash-like investments declined by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}.
Coverage: interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, so the buffer over debt service narrowed even as debt was repaid.
Traffic: growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}, which limits the scope for further operating leverage.

Regulation: the CNMC set the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged on the prior year, so aeronautical revenue per passenger of {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}} depends on traffic rather than tariffs.
